title: Joe Oliver's trumpet effects
summary: Garland describes 'Chork' Oliver's bad eye and wa-wa sounds made with a glass, derby and coffee can, and his hot, powerful playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Uh-uh. Right. That's what we want to get. How did you enjoy working with Joe Oliver?
All right. We was good buddies, then.
Was he a great, great player?
Old Chork was all right. (Unintelligible).
Right. Why did you call him Chork? (PHONETIC).
Because he had a bad eye.
A bad eye. Right. Did you hear him putting those different things into the trumpet?
Yes. He used a glass.
A glass. And someone said that he used a kazoo once, too.
He used a glass and he used a derby, most of the time it was setting on his head. Bought an old derby, and (Unintelligible). You know all that wa-wa business?
Yes.
He done that with a glass.
Uh-huh.
Then he got a can, an old coffee can.
And he used that, too. Did the audiences like that, the people?
Oh, my goodness, yes.
They went wild, huh? Did Oliver have a big range? A big style of playing, as we're told? I mean, did he really play big, powerful trumpet?
Oh, yeah.
Yeah. He was -- and he was a hot player.
He was a hot player, yes. (Held make all them funny things on his horn, unintelligible.)
